decision: Reject ETXTBSY/deny_write_access as a substitute for current executable SHA bookends.

verified.claim: deny_write_access is an inode-local signed counter, not a content seal attached to an arbitrary retained read-only FD.
Executable replacement releases write denial on the old image; original PID/start/group/sole Wait lifetime does not prove continuous executable lifetime.
Overlayfs documents a lower-layer executing-file case without ETXTBSY write/truncate denial.
Linux NFSv4 encodes share_deny as zero; local i_writecount is not a cross-client integrity seal.

limits: Source analysis only; no native bypass experiment or new filesystem mount performed.
A proposed A-to-B-to-A tail mutation may also change ctime, so do not claim all current metadata checks would accept it. Test the exclusion gap and record which existing guard actually refuses.
